theorem_title: An integer-valued Freiman 2-embedding of a finite set of reals
natural_language_statement:
For every finite set $X$ of reals there is a map $\varphi$ from $\mathbb{R}$ to $\mathbb{Z}$, injective on $X$, sending every solution of $a + b = c + d$ in $X$ to a solution of the same equation in $\mathbb{Z}$.

From the previous statement by clearing denominators: the functional takes finitely many rational values on $X$, so a single common denominator turns it into an integer-valued map, and scaling a linear map keeps it linear.
source: Folklore; the reduction from the reals to the integers in Janos Komlos, Miklos Sulyok, and Endre Szemeredi, "Linear problems in combinatorial number theory", Acta Math. Acad. Sci. Hungar. 26 (1975) 113-121
